rule: Weekly review flags when < 75% of running time over two weeks was easy (HR at or below Z2, i.e. <= 84% LTHR): an 80/20 intensity-distribution check that only starts a conversation.
summary: RCTs in trained and recreational runners found more gain with ~77-80% of time below VT1 than with ~47-67% (Esteve-Lanao 2007; Munoz 2014, the latter not significant overall), and a 120k-runner marathon dataset links a larger low-intensity share to faster times. Meta-analyses find polarized and pyramidal distributions roughly equal for time-trial performance (both are mostly easy); recreational athletes may do slightly better on pyramidal, so the flag should target too little easy running, not the shape of the hard work. 75% is a reasonable lower edge but not a tested cutoff; HR time-in-zone overcounts easy time during intervals (HR lag), and running is only part of this hybrid athlete's intensity load.

sources.note: Sub-elite runners, 5 months: 80.5% Z1 improved 10.4 km XC time more than 66.8% Z1 (-157 vs -122 s)
Recreational 10K runners: ~77% easy vs ~46% easy, 5.0% vs 3.6% gain, not significant overall; larger gain in the most-compliant subset
IPD network MA (13 studies): polarized = pyramidal for VO2max/TT; recreational athletes may respond better to pyramidal
Polarized slightly better for VO2peak (SMD 0.24), mainly highly trained/short studies; no TT difference
151k marathons: faster runners do more volume, mostly low intensity; Z1 share correlates with faster times; pyramidal most common
